forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Broxbourne Council to repay £51.65m borrowing within 12 months
news_drafts.lead: Broxbourne Council's entire £51.65m borrowing portfolio matures between April and September 2026, meaning the loans must be repaid and replaced—a concentration of debt repayment the council's treasury report describes as deliberate strategy to retain borrowing flexibility. The council's investment portfolio—money held in short-term investments to create an emergency financial cushion—has declined by £8m to £54m during the year. The available financial buffer against the borrowing has thus shrunk to £2.35m. The council generated £2.4m of investment income at a 4.25% average return during the year, according to the treasury management report, demonstrating active cash management despite the portfolio decline.

findings.paper_title: App B Overdue Tracker - Audit and Standards Committee
findings.headline: Multiple staffing recommendations delayed pending Local Government Reorganisation timeframe announcements
findings.detail: Recommendations on staffing strategy, benefits review, and use of fixed-term contracts are pending Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) timeframe decisions. This creates ongoing uncertainty around implementation timing for governance improvements related to staffing.
findings.matters: LGR uncertainty creates delays in finalizing staffing controls and prevents completion of audit responses on staffing governance
findings.figures: Two recommendations deferred pending LGR timeframes
findings.quote: The Assistant Director (Resources) is awaiting Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) timeframes to be announced in order to progress this forward.

findings.paper_title: App B Overdue Tracker - Audit and Standards Committee
findings.headline: Staff retention position has stabilized with no current recruitment or retention issues for senior posts
findings.detail: A March 2026 audit identified staff retention as a governance risk requiring action planning. By September 2026, the Strategic Risk Register has been reviewed and the council reports no current recruitment or retention challenges for senior positions.
findings.matters: Earlier staff retention risks could have threatened service continuity and governance capability; stabilization indicates successful resolution of a documented audit concern
findings.quote: The Council is not currently experiencing issues in recruitment or any current retention of senior posts.

findings.paper_title: App B Overdue Tracker - Audit and Standards Committee
findings.headline: Despite service charge reconciliation delays, council carries no service charge debt
findings.detail: Service charge money is ring-fenced for landlord services on specific estates. Budgets have not deviated significantly from estimates, with most tenants receiving small credits or small amounts due on next invoice. No service charge debt has accumulated despite the extended reconciliation delays.
findings.matters: Mitigates financial risk from delayed governance processes and shows underlying financial position on service charges remains sound despite administrative delays
findings.quote: Overall, there is no service charge debt. As service charge money is ring fenced for specific use for landlord's service for the estate being collected for, there is no effect on the Council funds, unless there is capital set aside for major works, but this would be refunded by tenants in due course.

findings.paper_title: App B Overdue Tracker - Audit and Standards Committee
findings.headline: Service charge reconciliation completion extended to November 2026, 17 months past June 2025 deadline
findings.detail: The May 2025 audit recommended completing all overdue service charge account reconciliations by 30 June 2025. As of September 2026, three property accounts (Depot, Old Building, Ingram House) are reconciled through 2024-25, but the New Building account remains outstanding.
findings.matters: Demonstrates pace of governance control implementation and underlying Finance team capacity constraints affecting basic financial processes
findings.figures: Original deadline 30 June 2025, current target 30 November 2026; three of four property accounts complete
findings.quote: The remaining outstanding work relates to the Bishops' College New Building account and resolving associated tenant queries.

findings.paper_title: App B Overdue Tracker - Audit and Standards Committee
findings.headline: High-priority IT Disaster Recovery plan 6 months overdue with testing deferred to March 2027
findings.detail: A high-priority February 2026 audit recommendation for a comprehensive IT Disaster Recovery plan remains incomplete as of September 2026. The design and master plan have been developed but technical documentation is still being finalized, with the first formal testing now targeted for 31 March 2027, nine months beyond the original deadline.
findings.matters: Disaster recovery capability is critical infrastructure risk for service continuity; extended delays on a high-priority control indicate governance risk management challenges
findings.figures: Original deadline 30 June 2026, revised to 31 December 2026, testing deferred to 31 March 2027
findings.quote: The remaining work is to resolve the technical documentation to finalise the Council's comprehensive IT Disaster Recovery Plan.
